searchText: Hey guys, quick question. When discussing ETH/Ether the currency in an article or story or whatnot what is the correct term to use? Should I use ETH or Ether? What is the policy you guys adhere to? (Putting in education as this is in relation to a book on Ethereum). I believe the terminology is "Ether is the currency, ETH is the ticker symbol". (I may be wrong here). Ether is the token which is a currency, asset, and a utility-based commodity. ETH is the ticker. Ethereum is the technology platform For Bitcoin, it's both the currency and the protocol I suppose. Whereas Ethereum is the protocol. Ethereum is more of a way of life tbh Like being vegan All ways of life are protocols 🙂 Haha yup Thanks guys! What I am trying to find out is should I use the currency (Ether) or ticker symbol (ETH)? They both refer to the same thing in different ways. From the ethereum.org Discord it seems more like ETH is more commonly used. Would that chime with people? What would you expect to see used in a book when discussing Ether/ETH?
